claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26, the Infrastructure Committee carried a motion reducing the time each approved public speaker could speak from the five minutes the Council Procedures Bylaw provides to a maximum of three minutes for that meeting, at a meeting for which about seventy people, between 60 and 80 entries on the committee's list, had been approved to speak on the bike-lane item.
claims.interpretation_notes: The committee's minutes record 64 approved-speaker entries for item 7.6, within the specified 60–80 band. The claim is supported under the brief's entry-based count. It is definition-sensitive if the count is instead the 52 entries recorded as presenting: that count is outside 60–80, so the queue-size element fails under that alternative. The minutes redact names, so distinct-person counts cannot be verified.

supporting_evidence.finding: Under item 1.4, the Infrastructure Committee carried M. Janz's motion setting a maximum of three minutes for each approved speaker at the August 26, 2026 meeting. All six listed committee members voted in favour. Under item 2.3, the committee approved speakers for item 7.6 in five panels with 15, 15, 15, 15 and 4 entries, totalling 64. The motion applied to each approved speaker, not only speakers on item 7.6.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The motion, mover, vote, outcome, scope and approved-speaker entries in the carried meeting record.
supporting_evidence.quote: each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of three minutes

supporting_evidence.finding: Section 38(1) sets the standing limit at five minutes for each approved speaker. The City-hosted PDF's indexed text states this limit; direct opening of the PDF returned a fetch error.
supporting_evidence.establishes: The standing five-minute limit that the committee modified.
supporting_evidence.quote: Each approved speaker may speak for a maximum of 5 minutes.

challenging_evidence.finding: The minutes record 52 public-speaker presentation entries under item 7.6, across four panels: 16, 16, 18 and 2. That figure is below the primary 60–80 band, so using speakers recorded as having presented instead of approved-speaker entries changes the queue-size result.
challenging_evidence.establishes: The required alternative count of entries recorded as presenting; it does not negate the approved-speaker count.

limitations: The City meeting portal returned 403 Forbidden when opened, and the City bylaw PDF returned 502 Bad Gateway. I used the complete selected minute items carried in this package and the official bylaw PDF text indexed in web search. The meeting items relevant to this claim were carried whole; names of members of the public were redacted.

The vote was 6–0, with all six committee members listed in attendance voting in favour. On the six-member attendance shown in the minutes, that exceeds the bylaw's two-thirds special-resolution threshold.

The time-limit motion was recorded under item 1.4, before the Requests to Speak motion at item 2.3 and before the first public presentation under item 7.6. The minutes also state under item 2.4 that item 7.6 was the first item of business.

The motion also set three minutes for each Council member to ask questions and three minutes to speak to or close debate on a motion. The carried minutes do not record speaker-specific extensions or actual speaking durations; the record therefore does not establish whether anyone spoke for more or less than the limit.
The minutes list five presentation attachments under item 7.6, with titles identifying public speakers withheld. The attachments are not reproduced here.

No reason for the motion is recorded in the carried minutes. I searched the meeting minutes and agenda and the indexed City record material consulted for this review; the minutes are not a record of debate or motive.

A web search of indexed City minutes surfaced earlier section 38 adjustments at City Council meetings on 2026-01-27, 2026-02-17 and 2026-03-17/18. This search was not an exhaustive review of every Council and committee minute since 2025-10-29.
unknowns: The number of distinct people represented by the redacted approved-speaker entries cannot be established from the carried text.
The carried text does not allow matching approved-speaker entries to presentation entries, so it cannot establish how many approved speakers did not present.
The minutes do not record each speaker's actual speaking duration or whether the limit was extended for an individual.

missing_evidence.description: Unredacted or consistently pseudonymized approved-speaker and presentation lists that permit matching entries across the lists and counting distinct people.
missing_evidence.likely_holder: City of Edmonton Office of the City Clerk

missing_evidence.description: A record of actual speaking durations or individual time extensions, if any.
missing_evidence.likely_holder: City of Edmonton Office of the City Clerk or meeting recording custodian

calculations_needed: Approved speakers on item 7.6: panel 1 = 15, panel 2 = 15, panel 3 = 15, panel 4 = 15, panel 5 = 4; N = 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 + 4 = 64 entries. Organizations: panel 1, Edmonton Bike Coalition and YEG Bike Coalition; panel 2, Bike Bus Alberta, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, YEG Bike Coalition, Paths for People, and Ward Métis Bikes (3 entries); panel 3, Let's Bike There YEG, Bike Edmonton and YEG Bike Coalition; panel 4, Paths for People and YEG Bike Coalition; panel 5, none. Total organization-bearing entries: 14.

N-all by item: item 7.1 = 5; item 7.3 = 1; item 7.4 = 8 in the original motion plus 1 additional speaker = 9; item 7.6 = 64. Total N-all = 5 + 1 + 9 + 64 = 79 entries. This counts entries, not distinct people, and counts the additional 7.4 entry once.

N-spoke on item 7.6: panel 1 = 16, panel 2 = 16, panel 3 = 18, panel 4 = 2; total = 52 entries. Organization-bearing entries: panel 1 = 5 (YEG Bike Coalition, Holyrood Voice, Holyrood Community 79 St Action Group, Paths for People, YEG Bike Coalition); panel 2 = 6 (Bike Bus Alberta, Ward Métis Bikes twice, Let's Bike There YEG, Bike Edmonton, Paths for People); panel 3 = 1 (YEG Bike Coalition); panel 4 = 0. Total organization-bearing entries: 12.

Primary band 60–80: N = 64, Supported; N-all = 79, Supported; N-spoke = 52, Partially supported because the queue-size element is outside the band. Alternative band 50–90: N = 64, Supported; N-all = 79, Supported; N-spoke = 52, Supported.
The item 1.4 vote was 6 in favour and 0 opposed, with six committee members listed as present. Two-thirds of six is four; 6 affirmative votes meet the special-resolution threshold.
For the main proposition, the standing limit is 5 minutes under section 38(1), and the motion set 3 minutes per approved speaker: a reduction of 2 minutes, calculated as 5 minus 3.
what_would_change_my_verdict: A corrected or later-approved meeting record changing the motion's outcome, its scope, the section 38 standing limit in force on 2026-08-26, or the approved-speaker entries for item 7.6 could change the primary verdict.
Using N-spoke instead of N changes the result to Partially supported under the primary 60–80 band, and to Supported under the alternative 50–90 band.
claims.suggested_one_line: The Infrastructure Committee carried a motion setting a three-minute maximum for every approved speaker, down from the bylaw's five minutes; 64 entries were approved for the bike-lane item, within the brief's about-seventy band. Counting only recorded presentations gives 52 entries and changes the result under the primary band.
